The attainment of this maximum size is a gradual process, and individuals may continue to add mass incrementally even after reaching skeletal maturity. This sexual size dimorphism is a consistent feature across populations and is maintained throughout the adult lifespan.

The entire life cycle of Cei (Phymaturus punae) unfolds against the backdrop of a remarkably slow life-history schedule, with individuals demonstrating exceptional longevity for a reptile of this body size. The extended lifespan allows for multiple reproductive events across an individual's lifetime, partially compensating for the exceedingly low annual fecundity. Such a bet-hedging strategy is typical of organisms inhabiting unpredictable or harsh environments, where the probability of juvenile survival is low and iteroparity with high adult survival is favored. The survival of adults from one year to the next is correspondingly very high.
